audit.whatIsWrong: Labelled EVEN at 5.5/10 while the data shows 57.65% over 1431 games with Ahri winning the first five rows.
audit.why: This is a favourable lane that becomes an unfavourable game — the difficulty label flattens that into 'even' and undersells how hard you should be pressing before his items.
audit.corrected: Chart aligned; diff label raised as a question rather than guessed at.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full chart read 'Skill' on all seven rows against content and packet reading Ahri x5 then Azir, Azir. whys[4] and content 'mid' also gave level 6 to Azir while win[4] said Ahri.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row, and whys[N] must agree with win[N].
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Ahri, phases[5..6].side -> Azir; whys[4] and 'mid' moved onto the Ahri side; phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to describe Azir's rows instead of Ahri's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this lane was absent: Charm instantly stops movement abilities, so it ends Shifting Sands mid-dash. Also missing — Shifting Sands halts on hitting a champion and immediately readies a new soldier, and Emperor's Divide is only 250 range, so he must come to you to cast it. wants.foe[0] credited soldiers with a shield they do not have; the shield is on Shifting Sands.
audit.why: Riot text for Charm: 'instantly stopping movement abilities'. Riot text for E: shields, dashes to a soldier, and 'if he hits an enemy champion, he instantly readies a new Sand Soldier and halts his dash'. R range is 250.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.carry, report[5].t, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, spikes[1].text, mid, wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block named a spell and no number, and the page never explained why his early poke is rationed.
audit.why: Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1 dropping to 6s; Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1; Arise! is 1.5s so soldiers restock almost instantly.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and spikes[0].text now carry the numbers.

audit.why: 'Snowball hard enough to end before his item spike' is the right win condition for a lane you win and a game you do not.

edits.before: Malignance spike: R cooldown drops and every dash window chains a full charm combo.
edits.after: His first item eases the mana that rationed him — soldier and shield uptime climb.

edits.before: Late Ahri is a pick machine: flank dash, charm the carry, and orb the body your team converges on.
edits.after: Late he is a teamfight engine: soldiers cover the ground and Emperor's Divide splits your team off.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by shielding through your burst with Shifting Sands and out-spacing you behind restocked soldiers.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Spirit Rush (last dash) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and is both his shield and his escape — while it is down he cannot leave a Charm. - Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1, so his poke is rationed early. - Arise! is 1.5s: killing soldiers buys seconds, never the trade.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry by charming the dash: Charm stops movement abilities outright, so Shifting Sands ends mid-flight and he lands next to you.

edits.before: Track Azir’s Shifting Sands: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Shifting Sands halts the moment it strikes a champion and hands him a fresh soldier — his escape turns into an engage if you body-block it.

edits.before: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 — bait it onto a soldier, count it down, then step up.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is only 250 range, so he must walk into your 975 Charm to cast it — hold E for that step and the wall never happens.

edits.before: Azir spends Shifting Sands early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Bank the ninth-minion heal on a full clear — his Q is 14s, so the wave is safe between casts.

edits.before: That is Azir’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Keep a dash — his wall is terrain and eats the ones you spent.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Stepping in while Shifting Sands is up hands him a shield through your burst and a free exit out of your combo.

edits.before: Level 6 tips to Azir as his ultimate wall threatens to split and disengage against you
edits.after: Level 6 stays yours as Charm stops Shifting Sands dead and his wall is only 250 range

edits.before: 2+ items favors Azir since his mana problems ease and soldier/shield uptime spikes hard
edits.after: First item favors Azir as his mana eases and Shifting Sands' 22s starts coming down

edits.before: Azir needs soldiers up to threaten a trade, and without a full wave he has no shield or damage, so you can punish his low-mana or low-soldier windows hard with Charm and full combo before he can Arise! back.
edits.after: Azir needs soldiers up to threaten a trade, and Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1, so between casts he has almost nothing — punish those windows with Charm and a full combo before Arise! restocks at 1.5s.

edits.before: His ultimate wall can body-block your Spirit Rush dashes and disengage attempts, but the cast time is long enough that you can often punish the commitment before the wall fully forms.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide knocks you back and leaves a wall that blocks your dashes, but it only reaches 250 — he has to come to you to cast it, and Charm at 975 answers that step-up before the wall exists.

edits.before: Level 6 slightly favors Azir since his ultimate wall can disrupt your positioning and split you from allies, but the long cast window still gives you a chance to punish the commitment with Spirit Rush before the wall fully forms, so it's close but tilts slightly toward him.
edits.after: Level 6 still favors you: Emperor's Divide reaches only 250, so he has to be close to use it, and Charm instantly stops movement abilities — his Shifting Sands exit dies mid-dash. Spirit Rush covers the knockback, so the wall costs him more than it costs you.

edits.before: Bait his ultimate before engaging fully
edits.after: Bait Shifting Sands before engaging

edits.before: Farm safely behind soldier shields until mana problems ease
edits.after: Farm safely behind soldiers until his mana problems ease

notes: The defining interaction of this lane — Charm 'instantly stopping movement abilities', which ends Shifting Sands mid-dash and strips Azir of both his shield timing and his escape — appeared nowhere on the page. Neither did the fact that Emperor's Divide is a 250-range cast, meaning he must enter Charm range to use it. The full-layer chart called all seven rows 'Skill' in a matchup Ahri wins at 57.65%, and whys[4] handed level 6 to Azir while the chart handed it to Ahri. wants.foe[0] also credited Sand Soldiers with a shield; the shield is on Shifting Sands.
